messages:
LinguaCorp: Hey @Ana — after the 2026-05-12 rollout (canary -> global, model v3.2.1, new quant/profile), our Spanish and Portuguese customers are getting mixed-language replies or full English responses when they explicitly request Spanish. Examples attached. This is impacting QA and a handful of paying customers.

LinguaCorp: Example 1 (request_id: rc_20260512_01):
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  \"input\": \"Traduce esto al español: ¿Cuál es la mejor manera de...\",
  \"model\": \"redwood-3.2.1\",
  \"user_locale\": \"es-ES\"
}
```
Response truncated: `...The best way is to...` (entirely English, no Spanish translation)

LinguaCorp: Example 2 (request_id: rc_20260512_07): user asked in pt-BR, model responded in English with an extra system-like instruction: `Note: you should...`

Ana (CS): Sorry — thanks for reporting. We're escalating. Can you paste the full curl (or three failing request_ids) and the timestamps? Also, did you see any HTTP 429/500s around those calls? Trying to see if fallback routing happened. :mag_right:

Marc (Support): Adding @Eva (Eng-ML) and SRE. Please include the exact headers (User-Agent, X-User-Locale if set). If possible, a minimal repro that hits hosted API would help.

sre-bot: Deploy canary -> global completed 2026-05-12 03:14:21 UTC for service inference-prod (release v2026.05.12.3).

Eva (Eng-ML): Quick notes from initial log scan: I grep'ed the logs for rc_20260512_*. I see a small number of requests routed to fallback model `redwood-3.1-fallback-en` due to a newly-introduced locale-compatibility check that mistakenly treats `pt-BR`/`es-419` as unsupported when the `user_locale` header is missing or malformed. This causes our routing policy to pick the English fallback.

Eva (Eng-ML): Probable cause: fallback policy change in the rollout that defaults to en-US when locale isn't normalized. Also saw ~12 requests with `kv_cache_hit: false` around the same window — not sure if related.

Marc (Support): Recommended immediate customer workaround: include `X-User-Locale: es-ES` (or `pt-BR`) header in the request, or set `generation.override_locale: \"es\"` in the payload. Ask them to try that and send 3 request_ids if it still fails.

Ana (CS): LinguaCorp — could you run one quick test with this curl and paste the response?
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <KEY>\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -H \"X-User-Locale: es-ES\" \
  -d '{"input":"Traduce esto al español: Hola, ¿cómo estás?","model":"redwood-3.2.1"}'
```

LinguaCorp: Sending three request_ids and timestamps: rc_20260512_01 (2026-05-12T03:18:02Z), rc_20260512_07 (2026-05-12T03:21:45Z), rc_20260512_12 (2026-05-12T03:26:10Z). We tested curl with X-User-Locale and that one returned Spanish correctly — so this matches your hypothesis (missing/normalized locale).

Eva (Eng-ML): Good repro, thanks. Short-term: we'll push a config override to treat common BCP47 variants as supported (es-*, pt-*) and avoid defaulting to en-US when header absent for the next 24h. Long-term: we need a normalization step in routing + unit tests for locale variants. I can push a hotfix canary tonight.

Marc (Support): Noted. I'll set this as P1 for CS escalation and update the customer with the workaround + ETA for a fix.

LinguaCorp: Thanks — appreciate the quick response. Please keep us posted, our product launch is stalled until this is resolved. :pray:

Ana (CS): I'll follow up with status updates here. If you see any 5xx/429s or odd latencies, please paste the request_id — could be related to traffic shaping too.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2789 (multilingual-routing-fallback). Assigned: eng-ml/eva. Priority: High.

Eva (Eng-ML): I'll post a link to the patch and deploy timeline once canary is running. Expected rollback/patch window: 2026-05-12 22:00 UTC.

Marc (Support): LinguaCorp — we'll follow up in the next 2 hours or when patch is live.

LinguaCorp: Got it, thanks all.
